newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Blast kills one in Tajik capital Dushanbe.
newsitem.headline: Blast kills one in Tajik capital Dushanbe.

text.p: An explosion next to the main post office in the centre of the Tajik capital Dushanbe killed one person and injured another on Thursday, witnesses said.

Reuters correspondent Yuri Kushko saw a corpse lying near the building and bystanders said an injured person had been taken to hospital. The blast smashed windows in nearby buildings hours after a ceasefire was due to come into effect in the former Soviet republic, which is wracked by civil war.
It was not immediately clear what caused the blast shortly after midday (0700 GMT). The building and surrounding area were quickly sealed off by police.

But nerves in the Tajik capital are on edge following a spate of attacks, widely blamed on opposition guerrillas, against Russian servicemen who help prop up Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov's shaky administration.

Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri agreed the ceasefire -- which was supposed to come into effect at midnight local time on Wednesday -- during talks in northern Afghanistan earlier this week in preparation for signing a peace agreement in Moscow on December 19.

But many previous accords have been routinely flouted in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China, despite efforts to end a four-year civil war which has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced many more.
